title: DKA 5 of 7, ICU: type 1 diabetes, SGLT2-inhibitor DKA with near-normal glucose, E. coli urosepsis and delirium (3 days, checkpoints every 0700 and 1900)
diagnosis: SGLT2-inhibitor-associated diabetic ketoacidosis with near-normal glucose (glucose 210, arterial pH 7.12, bicarbonate 9, anion gap 24, BHB 6.8) in type 1 diabetes of 52 years, with E. coli pyelonephritis and sepsis, delirium and acute kidney injury; potassium 3.3 with the insulin held, sulfonamide allergy, falls risk and an asymptomatic low glucose
desc: Thu 11/05 0700 to Sun 11/08 0700. A 67-year-old with type 1 diabetes on an SGLT2 inhibitor arrives confused with urosepsis and DKA although her glucose is only 210; care ends with a safe insulin plan and her daughter's teach-back. Vital signs after 0700 come from the bedside monitor.
